pref/digital_out_1/description: The device matches this name as an output before it reaches the preference table, so it is a device setting only, never a mode override.

pref/digital_out_4/description: The device matches this name as an output before it reaches the preference table, so it is a device setting only, never a mode override.
pref/enable_swap_inputs/label: Swap inputs with the side tube
pref/enable_swap_inputs/description: Swap the inputs using the side tube.
pref/enable_select_files/label: Select files with the side tube
pref/enable_select_files/description: Select a file using the side tube.
pref/enable_usb_a_device/risk: This picks which USB port the QuadStick presents itself on. The device tears USB down and reconnects when it changes, so a wrong value can leave it unseen by a console or computer. It also beats enable_usb_a_host: while this is set, the USB-A host stack is shut down whatever the host setting says. Change it only on advice from QuadStick support.
pref/enable_usb_a_host/description: Since firmware 2373. With this on and USB-A device mode off, the device runs a USB host on the USB-A port, so a controller plugged in there feeds the usb_1 input channels. Turn it off, or turn USB-A device mode on, and the host is torn down. USB-A device mode wins. QMP shows this as USB-A Host Mode.
pref/enable_DS3_emulation/description: Which USB device the QuadStick pretends to be. On firmware 2373: 0 QuadStick native, 1 DualShock 3, 2 x360ce, 3 Xbox 360, 4 DualShock 4 for a PS4, 5 Nintendo Switch Pro Controller, 6 DualShock 4 with no USB drive, 7 straight DS4 wireless. Value 5 meant PC only, no joystick on firmware 1476, so a file carrying 5 behaves completely differently once the device is updated. Modes 1, 5, 6 and 7 do not offer a USB drive at all, so a computer cannot see the QuadStick's files while one of them is running. QMP's Boot in PS4 Mode is value 4: firmware 2373 Joystick.c:625 calls that value "boot in PS4 mode" in its own comment.
pref/enable_DS3_emulation/risk: The name says DS3, but the device reads it as a USB emulation mode with eight numbered values, not an on or off switch. What 5 means changed between firmware 1476 and 2373, and a number the running firmware does not know leaves the device on an emulation nobody asked for. QCM keeps whatever is typed and refuses nothing, because a value that is wrong for one firmware is right for another. Change it only on advice from QuadStick support.
pref/enable_DS3_emulation/option/4: DualShock 4, for a PS4 (QMP's Boot in PS4 Mode)
pref/enable_DS3_emulation/option/5: Nintendo Switch Pro Controller, no USB drive
pref/usb_1_dead_zone/description: Since firmware 2373. Center dead zone for a controller plugged into the USB-A host port, counted in raw steps of that controller's centered axis byte, not in percent. Under the value the axis reads 0; over it the value is taken off so travel starts from zero, and the result is held to plus or minus 100. At 0 the axis passes through untouched. A centered axis byte only reaches about 127 either way, so 128 or more kills the axis.
pref/usb_2_dead_zone/description: Since firmware 2373, but the device ignores it. The name is legal and files carry it, yet nothing in the firmware reads the value: every USB host axis uses the USB 1 dead zone. Setting it in a mode row does nothing either.
pref/titan_two/description: Since firmware 2373. Tells the device it is reaching a PS4 through a Titan Two rather than plugged straight into the console. It then skips the DS4 authentication handshake and stops the periodic forced USB reconnect. QMP shows this as the Titan 2 PS4 flag.
pref/watchdog_disable/risk: The device runs a two minute hardware watchdog that restarts it if it stops responding. Nothing in firmware 1476 or 2373 reads this setting, so on either one it does nothing, and what a later firmware might do with it is unknown.
pref/debug/description: The device turns its console on when this is above zero.
